messages.subject_clean: Result of Fisher Exact Test and qValue
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

In some samples calculateDiffMeth function calculates p as zero and q value could be calculated as negative. It seems a bit strange to me. It may not be a big problem since both cases we can reject null hypothesis but I'll be pleased if anyone could tell me is there something wrong  or may be I miss something linked to default multiple test correction method of methylkit. Finally do you think is it ok to write a negative q Value to a paper or saying q >0.01 makes more sense.

Thanks,

Serbulent

messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] Result of Fisher Exact Test and qValue
messages.body_plain:
it is not expected to have negative q-values, p-values may appear as zero due to machine precision. If you are using the latest methylKit change use adjust="qvalue" method and see if it helps. If you are worried send a reproducible example. How you should present the statistics depends on journal policies, they might be OK with saying "q-value < 0.01"

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: function processBismarkAln - Update to version 1.0.0
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I was updated methylkit from 0.9.4 to 1.0.0 and run the processBismarkAln function.
I noticed that I didn't have the same average conversion rate between the 2 versions.

For example :

# version 1.0.0
processBismarkAln(location = "clean.tmp.sam" , sample.id <http://sample.id> = "tmp", assembly = "Galgal5", read.context = "CpG", save.folder = getwd(), mincov = 0)
# output :
6343 5626
total otherC considered (>95%% C+T): 11969
average conversion rate = 197.52376532058
total otherC considered (Forward) (>95%% C+T): 6343
average conversion rate (Forward) = 197.41988935561
total otherC considered (Reverse) (>95%% C+T): 5626
average conversion rate (Reverse) = 197.64087965505
Reading methylation percentage per base for sample: tmp

# version 0.9.4
processBismarkAln(location = "clean.tmp.sam" , sample.id <http://sample.id> = "tmp", assembly = "Galgal5", read.context = "CpG", save.folder = getwd(), mincov = 0)
# output :
6343 5626
total otherC considered (>95% C+T): 11969
average conversion rate = 98.7643869263913
total otherC considered (Forward) (>95% C+T): 6343
average conversion rate (Forward) = 98.7126530321065
total otherC considered (Reverse) (>95% C+T): 5626
average conversion rate (Reverse) = 98.8227139956143
Reading methylation percentage per base for sample: tmp

Why is it so different ?
This is the same input file.

Thanks in advance,

Marjorie

messages.subject: refseq.hg19.bed.txt
messages.body_plain:
Dear concerned Sir or Madame,
I followed the steps posted on your websites to get the hg19 annotation file
I went to the UCSC genome browser
Selected "Genes and Gene prediction tracks" from the "group" drop-down menu.
Selected the "Refseq Genes" from the "track" drop-down menu.
Selected "refGene" table
Selected "BED- browser extensible data" for the "output format".
Clicked "get output" and on the following page clicked "get BED" without changing any options.
Finally I saved the output as a text file

I tried this file with my dataset and it didn't give me the same result as the company who has done the same analysis on the dataset.

Here's my code:

gene.obj=readTranscriptFeatures("C:/Users/Sarah/Desktop/PhD_Research/methylKit/sarah.refseq.hg19.bed.txt")

diffAnn=annotateWithGeneParts(as(myDiff25p,"GRanges"),gene.obj,intersect.chr = TRUE)

head(getAssociationWithTSS(diffAnn))

The only inputs are myDiff25p and gene.obj

I got the same myDiff25p as the company so the only thing that can introduce discrepancy in the final result is  gene.obj.

Is there a standard refseq.hg19.bed.txt file? Can you help me spot what's wrong with my analysis?

Thank you so much!

All the best,
Sarah
